correctness.rationale: The exact finite transition generator, exposure concentration from exponential holding times and two-step harmonic mesh, independent exponential capture thresholds, vanishing probability of intermediate late defect captures, and deterministic parity correction prove convergence in total variation on a finite state space. The two-defect identity is an exact product. Standalone code passed 72 grouped checks, corroborative rather than an infinite proof.

evidence: The homogeneous monomer–dimer result yields a parity-repaired Poisson count; its uncapped channels cannot provide individual per-defect survival probabilities e^{-c_i}, nor rates c_i/sum c_j for terminal selection.

A fixed minority class on a complete tripartite adsorption graph instead has a folded binomial vacancy limit, owing to two growing independent classes and uniform deposition; its structure is not reducible to one ordinary clique plus nonadjacent weighted defects.
Two cliques connected by an extensive matching of bridge edges produce a Poisson bridge count; neither the graph nor the terminal set of vulnerable vertices coincides with this fixed-defect setup.

value.rationale: A naturally motivated rare-reactivity scale produces a full parameter-dependent labeled terminal law on an infinite family of dense adsorption networks. Fixed-capacity heterogeneous impurities yield an exact independent-survivor law plus nontrivial parity-selected competition at the final available ordinary site, together with a finite exact probability product. These are meaningful kinetic observables beyond adsorption density or the already-known scalar Poisson rare-event regime.
